history.dynasty: Ancient (legendary origin); structures built over centuries by noble and royal patrons
history.summary: NOT A TEMPLE - Vishram Ghat is a sacred bathing ghat (bath and worship place) on the banks of the Yamuna, not a temple; keep-or-drop decision needed for a temples dataset. It is the largest and most sacred of Mathura's 25 ghats. By popular tradition Lord Krishna rested ('vishram') here after killing the tyrant King Kansa, giving the ghat its name; the Varaha Purana instead says Vasudeva rested at the site (conflict). It is the traditional start and end point of the Braj Parikrama and the Mathura Panchkosi Parikrama; tradition holds the site was formerly a cremation ground, and the present structures were raised over the centuries by royal and noble patrons, with a reconstruction dated to 1814. The ghat is surrounded by centuries-old shrines including Mukut, Radha-Damodar, Murli Manohar, Neelkantheshwar, Yamuna-Krishna, Langali Hanuman and Narasimha temples. name: Vishram Ghat
town_description: Mathura is an ancient city on the banks of the Yamuna in the Braj region, revered as the birthplace of Lord Krishna and counted among Hinduism's Sapta Puri (seven holy cities). A major pilgrimage centre for millennia, it is dotted with temples, ghats and kunds, and lies about 160 km south-east of Delhi on the Delhi-Agra corridor.

travel.airport: Agra Airport (Kheria), about 70 km; Indira Gandhi International Airport, Delhi, about 160 km.
travel.railway: Mathura Junction, about 3 km from the ghat.
travel.road: In the old city on the Yamuna bank off Ramghat Road near Holi Gate; reachable by auto-rickshaw and cycle rickshaw; boat rides on the Yamuna are available.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; evenings for the Yamuna Aarti and floating diyas.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Open 24 hours (riverside ghat). Yamuna Aarti: summer 7:00 AM and 7:00 PM; winter 6:45 AM and 7:00 PM (per sanatanitraveller.com - verify locally).
